# Discovery-prep brief: Hyatt Hotels Corporation

Prepared 2026-10-25 for a first meeting. Every line cites its sources; lines the critic couldn't source were removed. Research by an AI agent from public web pages: check before quoting.

## Snapshot

- Hyatt Hotels Corporation was founded in 1957 and is headquartered at 150 North Riverside Plaza, Chicago, IL. [2]
- At December 31, 2025, Hyatt operated 1,528 properties and 372,763 rooms across 83 countries. [1]
- Full-year 2025 revenue was $7.10 billion, up 6.81% on 2024, with a net loss of $52 million attributable to the company (per a third-party summary of the FY2025 10-K). [1]
- The FY2025 annual report describes roughly 242,000 colleagues worldwide, with about 50,000 directly employed by Hyatt. [1]
- Class A shares are listed on the NYSE as H. The Pritzker family manages the business, per Wikipedia; the filing's ownership section was not checked, so share-class detail needs verification. [3]
- The brand portfolio spans full-service, select-service, lifestyle, and all-inclusive collections, with more than 40 brands named in a company profile (for example Park Hyatt, Andaz, Thompson Hotels, The Standard, and Hyatt Place). [2]

## Recent news (last 12 months)

- July 30, 2026: Q2 2026 results reported system-wide comparable hotel RevPAR up 5.9% versus Q2 2025, and a pipeline of about 154,000 rooms, up 10.0% year over year. Hyatt opened 3,585 rooms in Q2 2026. [5][6][7][8][9]
- May 2026: Investor Day gave an illustrative outlook through 2028 and a $1 billion increase in the share repurchase authorization. [8][10][11]
- January 2026: Hyatt finished 2025 with its highest number of U.S. room signings in five years and a record global pipeline of about 148,000 rooms. [8][10][11]
- February 2026: the CEO said Hyatt rebuilt its website search engine to reflect how travelers plan trips. [24][25][26]
- March 2026: Skift reported that Hyatt.com search was rebuilt around generative AI, so travelers can search by intent such as climate or amenities. [29]
- April 2026: Hyatt reported it was using ChatGPT Enterprise for content creation and support communications across social, owner, and operator audiences. [24][25][26]
- July 2026: Power's study ranked Hyatt House first in upscale extended stay for a fifth consecutive year. [21]
- Upcoming: Q3 2026 results are scheduled for Thursday, October 29, 2026, before the market opens. They are not yet available. [12][13]

## What guests say (themes)

- Room condition and cleanliness are a frequent complaint, including dated rooms, weak air conditioning, dirty bathrooms, and stained bedding. [15][16]
- Breakfast is a recurring target, described as not competitive and costing $11 at one property, and as unkempt or subpar in 2026 reviews. [16][17][18]
- High fees and unexpected charges are a common complaint, and value for price draws criticism. [17][19]
- Loyalty redemption and website booking problems appear in 2026 reviews, and digital check-in scores lower than peers. [19]
- Staff experience is mixed: some reviewers praise staff as excellent and responsive, while others report weak professionalism, especially overnight. [14][15]

## Technology hints

- Reservations: in July 2023 Hyatt announced Sabre's SynXis as its main central reservation system from 2024. The rollout status was not confirmed in the findings. [22]
- Revenue management: Hyatt PrO is a global collaboration with IDeaS, and revenue leaders use proprietary software for automation and rate management. [22][27]
- Earlier commitment to MaximRMS predictive analytics for pricing. Its current status is not confirmed. [28]
- Experiences: the Way platform is integrated across Hyatt.com, the World of Hyatt app, and property sites, with APIs described as planned or in progress. Current status is unclear. [22][23]
- AI: Hyatt launched a Hyatt-branded application within ChatGPT, uses ChatGPT Enterprise internally, and has licensed Microsoft and Anthropic for agentic platforms it built. [24][25][26]

## Ten questions for the meeting

1. Which systems hold the rate, inventory, and pricing data that revenue leaders use today, and how do franchised hotels get that data?
2. Since the SynXis rollout was announced for 2024, what is its current status across owned, managed, and franchised hotels?
3. What does a typical revenue manager do each week, and which of those steps take the most time?
4. How are the proprietary revenue management tools and MaximRMS, or their successors, used in practice, and where do they fall short?
5. Where do guest complaints about cleanliness and room condition get recorded, and who acts on them at the property level?
6. How are breakfast and fee complaints tracked, and who owns the decision on breakfast pricing and fee policy?
7. When a guest has trouble redeeming rewards or booking on the website, what is the path to resolution, and where are those cases logged?
8. What did the rebuilt Hyatt.com search change in measurable terms, such as conversion or search-to-booking rate, and what remains manual?
9. How does ChatGPT Enterprise fit with the owner and operator communication workflows, and what approvals does it require?
10. What is the current state of the Way platform integration, and which team owns the APIs that property websites depend on?

## Three use-case hypotheses (4-check test)

| Use case | Why | Felt | Would pay | Buildable in a week | First user known |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Revenue management copilot for managed and franchised hotels | Revenue management is the clearest operational lever in the findings. Hyatt says it maximizes revenue through a dedicated team, serves franchisees on request, and states goals of faster response to competitive actions and demand changes. [27][28] | Unknown | Unknown | Unknown | Probably |
| Guest review triage for property operations | Guest complaints about cleanliness, room condition, breakfast, and fees recur across reviews and third-party analyses. A tool could group these issues by property and theme so operations teams can act on them. [15][16][17][18][19][20] | Yes | Unknown | Probably | Unknown |
| Loyalty and booking support assistant | Reviews report redemption and website booking trouble, and digital check-in scores lag peers. Loyalty is described as the main personalization data source, so an assistant could resolve common issues using that data. [19][24][25][26][27][31] | Probably | Unknown | Unknown | Unknown |

## Outreach email

> Hi, I'm Vamsi, an engineer working on applied AI for hotel operations. I'd like to ask for 30 minutes to learn how your teams handle revenue management, guest feedback, and loyalty support today, and where the current tools fall short. I'm not coming with a product pitch. I'd like to understand the problems first and see whether an engineering partnership makes sense. Would you be open to a discovery call in the next few weeks? I can work around your schedule. Thank you for considering it. Vamsi

# Discovery-prep brief: Club Med

Prepared 2026-10-25 for a first meeting. Every line cites its sources; lines the critic couldn't source were removed. Research by an AI agent from public web pages: check before quoting.

## Snapshot

- Club Med is a French travel operator founded in 1950, headquartered in Paris, specializing in all-inclusive holidays; primarily owned by Fosun Group since 2013. [1]
- Headcount estimates conflict widely (14,560; 20,333; 28,000), so no single figure should be used. [1][2][3][4][5]
- Footprint is in dispute: one source says nearly 70 resorts in 30 countries, another lists 59 all-inclusive resorts in 2026, and no authoritative current count was found. [3][4][5][6][7]
- Mountain/ski resorts are a significant part of the portfolio, with sources citing 20 to 25+ on-snow resorts depending on the page. [6][7][8][9]
- Public information about internal operations and systems is thin; the basics (resort count, system landscape, ownership of operations data) need confirmation in the meeting. [6][7][10][11][25]

## Recent news (last 12 months)

- 21 April 2026: Club Med's corporate news page reports 2025 results and an inaugurated first resort in South Africa (Beach & Safari), with another South Africa opening listed for July or September 2026. [10][11][14]
- 2025 was described by the company as a landmark year, reaching an all-time high in Business Volume and Resort Operating Income. [13]
- Club Med Borneo is set to open in November 2026, a 400-key rainforest property, with bookings launched March 24, 2026. [10][13][14][15]
- Club Med announced a return to the U.S. market through acquisition and redevelopment of the Carambola Beach Resort in St. Croix, with VICI Properties (date not confirmed). [3][4][5]
- Property deals signed in Indonesia (Manado) and Thailand (Koh Samui, with Central Group Capital); dates not confirmed. [10][13]
- A Québec ski resort is scheduled to open in December 2028. [12]

## What guests say (themes)

- Service is praised, especially for children and warm, attentive staff, though consistency varies by resort. [16][17]
- Food is often praised but criticized for limited variety and repeated menu items. [17][18][19]
- Rooms and facilities are a recurring weak spot, described as dated. [18][19][20]
- Value for money is split; some find all-inclusive worthwhile while others warn of extra costs. [16][17]

## Technology hints

- Loyalty program has tiered statuses (Turquoise to Platinum) with thresholds that differ by market, plus a 'My Club Med App' for members. [21][22]
- Pay-over-time checkout is provided through a partnership with Uplift on all reservations. [23]
- Algolia powers search across the global website. [24]
- A third-party directory lists a 'Club Med – PMS' version 8.0, though this is unverified. [25]
- Customer contact centre uses AI analysis of calls and chats, and a Microsoft partnership covers AI-powered guest experiences and cloud modernisation. [27][28][29][30]

## Ten questions for the meeting

1. What is the current official number of resorts and how do you count them: all-inclusive, owned, managed, or franchised?
2. Which booking engine and property management system do you run, and is the 'Club Med – PMS' listing accurate?
3. How are resort operations data (occupancy, pricing, guest feedback) collected and where do they live today?
4. How do the Uplift, Algolia and Microsoft integrations connect to your core booking and loyalty systems?
5. What is the process when a guest complaint about rooms or facilities is raised, and who owns the fix?
6. How are food variety and menu rotation planned and measured across resorts?
7. How is the value-for-money perception tracked, and where do the extra-cost complaints come from?
8. How is staff assignment handled today, and how does G.O Match fit into scheduling and mobility decisions?
9. What does the contact centre quality scoring do with its analysis, and where do supervisors see the gaps?
10. Which new resort openings (Borneo, South Africa, Manado, Koh Samui, Carambola) will need new systems or data flows first, and who owns that rollout?

## Three use-case hypotheses (4-check test)

| Use case | Why | Felt | Would pay | Buildable in a week | First user known |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| AI analysis of guest feedback to find recurring resort issues | Reviews repeatedly flag service, food variety, rooms and value; the company already analyzes calls and chats, so a similar pipeline for reviews may help prioritize fixes. [16][17][18][19][20][29][30] | Probably | Unknown | Probably | Unknown |
| AI-assisted staff scheduling and skills matching for resorts | G.O Match already automates staff assignments; new resorts opening in 2026 and 2028 may create staffing demand, but the gap is not documented. [10][11][12][27][28] | Unknown | Unknown | No | Unknown |
| Guest-facing conversational assistant for researching properties | The company stated in February 2024 it planned a conversational experience for customers in select markets to help them research properties; Algolia search is in place but may not meet that need. [24][27][28] | Unknown | Unknown | Unknown | Unknown |

## Outreach email

> Hello, I am Vamsi, an engineer working on forward-deployed software projects. I am reaching out because Club Med has a wide range of public announcements in 2026, including new resorts in South Africa, Borneo and Manado, and a return to the U.S. market with Carambola. I would like to understand how your teams handle guest feedback, staff scheduling and booking systems in practice. Would you be open to a 30-minute discovery call in the next few weeks? I can work around your schedule. Thank you for considering it. Vamsi

# Discovery-prep brief: Four Seasons Hotels and Resorts

Prepared 2026-10-25 for a first meeting. Every line cites its sources; lines the critic couldn't source were removed. Research by an AI agent from public web pages: check before quoting.

## Snapshot

- Four Seasons Hotels and Resorts is privately held, headquartered in Toronto, Ontario, Canada; it operates 135 hotels and resorts and 61 residences in 47 countries per its own 2026 press release. [1][4][11]
- Ownership: Cascade Investment, L.L.C. holds a controlling 71.25% stake; Kingdom Holding Company retains 23.75%; founder Isadore Sharp holds 5% through Triples Holdings Limited. [1][2]
- Cascade's increase from 47.5% to 71.25% was announced in 2021 (Cascade bought half of Kingdom Holding's stake for $2.21 billion) and completed in January 2022. [2][3]
- No reliable, complete 2026 brand list was found, so the brands operated are unverified. [4]
- Counts vary by date; a 2025 trade report gave 133 properties, so 135 is the most recent figure found. [8]

## Recent news (last 12 months)

- May 2026: Four Seasons named Robert Fritz Executive Chairman; founder Isadore Sharp will assume the role of Chairman Emeritus. [9]
- April 29, 2026: The Tokyo at Marunouchi hotel, after a transformative renovation, began taking reservations. [9]
- Monday, May 18, 2026: Louis reopens after a multi-million-dollar renovation. [10][11]
- January 2026: The company said it will advance its global pipeline through growth across Italy, Greece, and Saudi Arabia. [10][11]
- October 2026: A development update disclosed 13 upcoming hotel and resort openings and reopenings across Europe, the Americas, Africa, the Middle East and Asia. [26]
- Gap: no signed management deals or financial results were found for October 2025 to October 2026. [11]

## What guests say (themes)

- Service is the most praised theme; guests often describe staff as attentive, and some say service exceeds expectations in Las Vegas. [12]
- Check-in and service lapses recur, including slow arrivals (one guest reported 20 minutes at check-in in Las Vegas) and a New York review of repeated card declines at check-in. [13][14]
- Pricing and fees draw criticism, including extra fees and high dining costs in Las Vegas and an automatic 20% service fee at the Denver pool and spa. [12][15]
- Spas and dining are often praised, including Kuala Lumpur spa reviews and Atlanta health club/spa reviews. [16][17]
- Room condition is mixed: cleanliness is frequently praised, but some guests criticize dated bathrooms or noise. [12][18]

## Technology hints

- The web platform is Adobe, which drives the digital experience. [19]
- Enterprise SaaS includes Salesforce and Workday; the source list is cut off, so it may be longer. [19]
- Guest app lets guests make and manage reservations and view itineraries; chat is staffed by people rather than bots, per the company's 2020 release. [19][20]
- Canary Technologies (vendor claim) lists Four Seasons among hotel brands using its guest management platform. [20][21]
- A centralized guest profile system informs anticipatory service across properties and channels. [25]

## Ten questions for the meeting

1. Which brands and property types (resort vs. city hotel) are in the portfolio today, and which systems hold each property's reservations and guest profiles?
2. How is the centralized guest profile system structured, who owns it, and how is preference data updated after a stay?
3. What is the current chat volume across properties, and how is it routed between staff and the app today?
4. How are the 3.5 million-plus chat messages (reported in 2018) handled now, and what share is requests like extra towels or airport pickups?
5. Where does check-in friction come from (card declines, property systems, staffing), and which properties measure arrival time?
6. How are service fees, such as the 20% automatic charge at pool and spa, set and disclosed across properties?
7. How do the Adobe, Salesforce, and Workday platforms connect to property management and guest management systems like Canary?
8. Which of the 13 upcoming openings and reopenings in the October 2026 update need systems set up before opening, and who leads that work?
9. How do property teams prepare for guest arrivals today, and what information do they wish they had in advance?
10. Who in operations, IT, and guest services would own a pilot, and what would success look like for them in the first 30 days?

## Three use-case hypotheses (4-check test)

| Use case | Why | Felt | Would pay | Buildable in a week | First user known |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Guest request triage in the app chat | Chat is staffed by people and guests send many routine requests, so automated triage could route requests faster. [20][22][23] | Probably | Unknown | Unknown | Unknown |
| Pre-arrival preparation from guest profiles | Executives want to prepare in advance and personalize amenities from preference data, and a central profile system exists. [24][25] | Probably | Unknown | Unknown | Unknown |
| Check-in friction reduction | Guests repeatedly report slow or problematic check-ins, including card declines. [13][14] | Probably | Unknown | Unknown | Unknown |

## Outreach email

> Hi, I'm Vamsi. I'm preparing for a conversation with Four Seasons about how teams handle guest requests, pre-arrival preparation, and check-in operations across properties. Your 2026 release reports 135 hotels and resorts and 61 residences in 47 countries, and the October 2026 update lists 13 upcoming openings and reopenings. Would you be open to a 30-minute discovery call in the next two weeks to learn how your teams work today and whether any of it is worth a focused pilot? I'd come with questions, not a proposal. Thanks, Vamsi

# Discovery-prep brief: Sandals Resorts International

Prepared 2026-10-25 for a first meeting. Every line cites its sources; lines the critic couldn't source were removed. Research by an AI agent from public web pages: check before quoting.

## Snapshot

- Sandals Resorts International (SRI) is the parent company of the Sandals, Beaches, and Grand Pineapple Beach Resorts brands, and also runs Fowl Cay Resort and several private villas. [1][2]
- Headquarters are in Montego Bay, Jamaica, at 5 Kent Ave. [3]
- The company is privately held by the Stewart family. Royal Caribbean Group's reported 50% stake for about $3 billion is pending and unverified, with closing expected in early 2027. [2][4][12]
- Sandals has 17 beachfront resorts across Jamaica, Antigua, Saint Lucia, The Bahamas, Barbados, Grenada, Curacao, and Saint Vincent and The Grenadines. Jamaica has the most, with seven. [2][7]
- Headcount differs by source: about 13,324 (Revelio Labs, March 2026), about 5.7K (LeadIQ, July 2026), and 10,001+ (LinkedIn). [1][5][6]
- Sandals is adults-only for couples and enforces an 18+ policy at every property, while Beaches welcomes families. [8][11]

## Recent news (last 12 months)

- March 2026: SRI announced a US$200 million reimagining of Sandals Montego Bay, Sandals Royal Caribbean, and Sandals South Coast, with reopenings pushed later in 2026. [13]
- Phased reopening begins with Sandals South Coast on Nov. 18 (year not stated in the source), followed by Sandals Royal Caribbean and Sandals Montego Bay in December. [13]
- June 2026: Sandals Royal Caribbean is being rebranded as Sandals Caribbean Cay, adding 84 rooms for 291 accommodations. [13][14]
- September 22, 2026: Wikipedia reports the Royal Caribbean 50% stake announcement. A fan blog described the deal as close, and the final terms are unverified. [2][15][16]
- October 19, 2026: Travelweek reported that the two companies are preparing cruise-and-stay packages. Sandals said it has no plans to discontinue its travel advisor programs. [16][17]
- October 21, 2026: Sandals renamed 15 best-selling products, for example Sandals Royal Bahamian is now Sandals Bahamas Nassau. [16][17]

## What guests say (themes)

- Reviews are overwhelmingly positive, especially about friendly, attentive staff. [18]
- Recurring complaints involve slow or understaffed service: slow restaurant service, understaffed bars at busy times, and weak daytime service and dining options outside dinner. [19][20][21]
- Room condition is a recurring complaint, with maintenance problems and rooms that read as dated. [21][22]
- Guests cite high prices relative to luxury expectations as a complaint. [22][23]

## Technology hints

- Unique Travel Corp, the worldwide representative of Sandals and Beaches, chose IBS Software's iStay platform to replace its central reservation system (2024 announcement). [24]
- IDeaS, a SAS company, partnered with Unique Vacations Inc. in 2022 on AI-based revenue planning. [24][25]
- The Island Insiders Club loyalty program runs through the Sandals and Beaches app and a dedicated booking engine. [26][27]
- Sandals Specialist (sandalsspecialist.com) is the travel agent booking portal. [28]
- Guest requests have run through a QR-code system since 2014, with staff alerted to guest requests. [30][31]
- The company uses AI and augmented reality in staff training through a partnership. [34]

## Ten questions for the meeting

1. Which systems hold reservations, guest profiles, and loyalty data today, and how do they connect after the iStay CRS replacement?
2. How far has the move to one unified system across the 17 properties progressed, and which properties are still on the old setup?
3. What data silos does the IT team see, and what administrative work do they cause for property staff?
4. How does the QR-code request system route requests today, and what is the average time from request to fulfillment?
5. Where do room-service and room-delivery delays happen most often, and how is that measured?
6. How are staffing levels set for bars and restaurants during peak periods, and what has changed since the reviews?
7. How is guest personalization handled at online check-in, such as recording anniversaries, and who owns that data?
8. What does the Royal Caribbean deal change operationally for systems, data sharing, and the cruise-and-stay packages, and what is not yet known?
9. How do the reimagined Montego Bay, Royal Caribbean, and South Coast reopenings affect systems, staffing, and go-live timing?
10. Who would own a pilot project, what budget and success measures would apply, and what would make you stop?

## Three use-case hypotheses (4-check test)

| Use case | Why | Felt | Would pay | Buildable in a week | First user known |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Guest request and service-recovery triage | Guests already send requests through a QR system, but reviews report slow fulfillment, so routing and prioritizing requests may reduce wait times. [30][31][32][33] | Yes | Unknown | Unknown | Unknown |
| Pre-arrival personalization from booking and loyalty data | A guest reported that a noted anniversary during online check-in was ignored, and the app and booking engine already hold the data that could drive personalization. [23][26][27] | Probably | Unknown | Unknown | Unknown |
| Unified guest and reservation data layer across properties | A group IT director described data silos and extra administrative work, and the company is moving to a single CRS and unified system, so a shared data layer could support the migration. [24][29] | Probably | Unknown | No | Unknown |

## Outreach email

> Hello,
>
> I work on applied AI for hospitality operations and would like to learn how Sandals Resorts International approaches guest service and data work across its properties. I am asking for a 30-minute discovery call to hear your priorities and understand where a small, practical pilot could fit, if at all.
>
> The reason for reaching out is the public record: the move to a unified reservation system, the QR-based guest request process, and the reimagined resorts reopening this season. I would like to understand what is working and what is not from your side.
>
> Would you be open to a 30-minute call in the next two weeks? I can work around your schedule.
>
> Thanks,
> Vamsi
